item.description: El único caso del virus Shamonda detectado en humanos corresponde a un paciente con una enfermedad grave en el sistema inmunitario que murió a inicios de octubre. El Centro Europeo para la Prevención y el Control de Enfermedades explicó que la víctima era más proclive a infecciones que la población general e informó de investigaciones para determinar "si el virus causó o contribuyó a su muerte y cómo adquirió la infección". Las autoridades no ven ningún riesgo para la salud pública. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Webb image reveals young stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
item.description: In this Picture of the Month from the NASA/ESA James Webb Space Telescope, we visit a turbulent cauldron of star formation to see what is brewing inside dense clumps of gas. This is a star-forming region named LHA 120-N 159, or simply N159, located 161,000 light-years away in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), one of the satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way galaxy. This image spans about 230 light-years across. Publicado también por: European Space Agency. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists turn art detectives to date van Gogh's 'Starry Night' to actual sky from 1889
item.description: A team of South Korean researchers has put forward a new date for the night sky depicted in Dutch painter Vincent van Gogh's famed masterpiece "The Starry Night". Art historians have long assumed the stars were a product of the artist's fantasy or dated the scene to June 1889 based on the artist's location and other details, but astronomical details like the sliver crescent moon don't line up. item.title: Ukraine and Russia exchange strikes after US envoy visit to the Kremlin
item.description: Ukraine and Russia exchanged drone and missile strikes on Thursday, killing seven people in Ukraine, according to authorities. item.title: Shamonda virus detected in human for first time in France
item.description: Investigations under way to determine whether virus normally found in livestock contributed to man’s death A man in France has become the first human known to have contracted Shamonda virus, with investigations under way to explore whether it contributed to his death. Shamonda virus is a type of bunyavirus and is spread by bites from infected midges. According to the Austrian Agency for Health and Food Safety , in animals such as cattle, sheep and goats it can cause diarrhoea, lack of appetite and a decline in milk yield, “as well as abortions and congenital abnormalities in newborn calves… Publicado también por: BBC News - World. item.title: Indonesia: humo tóxico, corrupción y protestas por los incendios
item.description: Indonesia afronta una de sus peores crisis de incendios forestales en más de una década. El humo tóxico ha provocado cientos de miles de afecciones respiratorias, alterado los vuelos y obligado a cerrar escuelas, mientras la contaminación se extiende a países vecinos como Malasia y Singapur. La emergencia coincide con protestas contra la gestión del Gobierno y una investigación por presunta corrupción en la contratación de fondos de emergencia. ¿Qué está detrás de los incendios y qué puede hacer Yakarta para frenar una crisis que afecta a toda la región? item.title: Amy Winehouse: Back to Black 20 review – trying an all-star Amy tribute show is a losing game
item.description: (Roundhouse, London) With Jorja Smith, Mark Ronson and others reinterpreting Back to Black for its 20th anniversary, most of the singers are eclipsed by the memory of Winehouse It’s 20 years since Amy Winehouse released her masterpiece Back to Black and 15 since she died at a frighteningly young age. A good way to appreciate how special she was is to watch the Amy Winehouse Band trot through a few lesser songs and cover versions and spot what’s missing: her playfulness, bite, anarchic charisma and taste. item.title: What is happening in France? Unpacking the recent waves of protests
item.description: Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Dr. Laura Keesman, Assistant Professor of Sociology at the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. Dr. Keesman examines the complex relationship between peaceful protest, radical activism, social inequality and state authority. She challenges the tendency to interpret disruptive demonstrations exclusively through the lens of extremism. Even when protesters engage in confrontational or unlawful actions, she argues, their motivations may remain rooted in genuine political and socioeconomic grievances. Fuente: France 24 - English.
